name: Printing the Total Number of Times Elements of One Array Appear in Another Array
description: Construct a program that has a method that receives two arrays and prints the total number of times the elements in the 2nd array appear in the 1st array. For example, if the 1st array is {1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6} and the 2nd array is {3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, then the total number of times that the elements in the 2nd array appear in the 1st array is 6.\nNote that we need to count matches for all values in the 2nd array (including duplicate values, if any).

comments.content: This statement declares the method searchArrays that takes two arrays and prints the total number of times elements in the 2nd array appear in the 1st array.
We need variable count to count how many times the elements in the 2nd array appear in the 1st array. We initialize count with 0 because we have not started counting yet.

We want to iterate over the 2nd array (lst2) and count the total number of times its elements appear in the 1st array. To do this, we need use nested for loops. The outer for loop iterates over the elements in the 2nd array while the inner for loop traverses the elements in the 1st array and increments the total number of matches by 1 each time that a match is found between the elements in the two arrays.

This statement is the outer for loop in the nested loop.

The outer for loop is a for-each statement that assigns the name val2 to each of the elements in the 2nd array in turn, from left to right, and the statements inside the outer loop body will be executed for each.

This statement is the inner for loop in the nested loop. It's a for-each statement that assigns the name val1 to each of the elements in the 1st array in turn, from left to right, and the statements inside the inner loop body will be executed for each.
We check whether val1 from the 1st array and val2 from the 2nd array are equal by using the == operator. The if evaluates to true if val2 is equal to val1 and false otherwise.
If val1 is equal to val2, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
We increment the total number of matches stored in variable count by 1 if we find a match between the values in the two arrays.
The += operator adds 1 to the value of variable count and the result is stored back into the variable count. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement count = count + 1.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the total number of times elements in the 2nd array appear in the 1st array.

The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character.

We define array referred by variable values1 to hold the elements of the 1st array. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }. Note that the array is of type double because we want to store floating-points numbers in the array.

We define array referred by variable values2 to hold the elements of the 2nd array. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }. Note that the array is of type double because we want to store floating-points numbers in the array.
This statement calls the searchArrays method and passes the 1st array and the 2nd array as its arguments.
